subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: Should aborted no-output GitHub Copilot Claude cron runs be treated as model-fallback-worthy by default, and should that policy be generic or Copilot-specific?
rationale: Current source shows a partial fix plus an explicit aborted-result fallback exclusion; changing that policy can retry after local aborts and may duplicate side effects.

options.title: Generic invisible-abort fallback
options.body: Classify aborted embedded runs with no assistant text, no tool calls, and no committed delivery as retryable while preserving safeguards for user cancellations and delivered side effects.

options.title: Copilot-only transport handling
options.body: Add a Copilot anthropic-messages idle or first-token timeout/error conversion without changing generic aborted-result fallback policy.

options.title: Require live repro first
options.body: Keep source unchanged until a maintainer or QA lane reproduces the Copilot Claude stall on current main with redacted logs.

recommendation.title: Generic invisible-abort fallback
recommendation.body: Classify aborted embedded runs with no assistant text, no tool calls, and no committed delivery as retryable while preserving safeguards for user cancellations and delivered side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the Copilot Claude transport and provider behavior implicated by the remaining decision.
